attempts.label: DANDI:000686
attempts.paper_title: Next generation CANCAN focusing for remote stimulation by nanosecond electric pulses
attempts.entry_title: Next generation CANCAN focusing of electroporation (Pakhomov et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: Few of the paper's findings on CANCAN focusing held up fully in this data. Lifting the electrodes 2 mm above the cells raised targeting of the array's centre as reported, and more packets or a higher amplitude raised uptake, though amplitude by about 6 to 7 times where the paper gives about 16, and uptake was not restricted to the centre. Packet 2 did not give the best targeting; the dishes labelled Packet 3 did. Whether rotation creates a central peak and whether targeting is independent of amplitude and array size could not be settled, as the result depends on an ROI layout the paper does not describe. The single-cell cancellation experiments and field simulations are in no dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the monolayer findings of Pakhomov, Gudvangen, Mangalanathan, Kondratiev, Redondo and Semenov (2023) on dandisets 000686, 000875, 001025, 001027 and 001028, which hold the stitched YO-PRO-1 images of the CHO monolayers of Figures 5 to 9, one dish per file. The electrode squares are found in the images and the ROIs of Methods 2.4 are rebuilt from them. The single-cell time lapse of Figure 4 and the field simulations of Figure 3 are in none of the datasets.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pakhomov et al. (2023) from dandisets 000686, 000875, 001025, 001027 and 001028
Findings of the earlier attempt pakhomov-2023-04, checked on dandiset 001027

outcomes.statement: In the simulations, 1 kV applied to one electrode gives about 1.8 kV/cm in the center of the small array and 0.8 kV/cm in the center of the large array, and about 4-fold more near the energized electrode (7 and 3.5 kV/cm per kV). Energizing one diagonal gives no field in the center.
outcomes.quote: For example, applying 1 kV to one electrode produced the electric field of approximately 1.8 kV/cm and 0.8 kV/cm in center of the small and large arrays ... The electric field strength was about 4-fold higher near the energized electrode (7 kV/cm and 3.5 kV/cm per 1 kV applied, for the small and large arrays, respectively) Note that energizing either electrode diagonal produced no electric field in the center of the array
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the paper's Sim4Life field maps. None of the five dandisets holds them; every file holds one or two still images of a monolayer (ImageSeries ScanningImaging, 70 files). The paper deposits no model output elsewhere and links no code or data.

outcomes.statement: Sham-exposed cells gain no YP fluorescence over the 10 min of imaging, while cells given pulses show a gradual rise in YP signal from the first image after exposure.
outcomes.quote: Sham-exposed cells showed no gain in YP fluorescence during the 10 min of observation. In contrast, cells treated by electric pulses displayed gradual increase in YP signal, starting from the image frame taken immediately after nsEP exposure.
outcomes.notes: The single-cell time lapse of Fig. 4 (images every 10 s for 600 s, Methods 2.2) is in none of the five dandisets, whose 70 files each hold one stitched monolayer image (two channels in 17 of them) and no time series. The paper names no other location.

outcomes.statement: A single 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm causes by far the strongest YP uptake, 126 +/- 14 a.u. (n = 25 cells) by the end of recording.
outcomes.quote: A single 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm caused by far the strongest YP uptake, reaching 126±14 a.u. (n=25) by the end of recording.
outcomes.notes: As fig4-sham-no-uptake, the single-cell data of Fig. 4 are in none of the datasets.

outcomes.statement: Bipolar signals that start with the same pulse cause significantly weaker uptake (p < 0.001). By the end of recording the 4-phasic signal reaches 20.8 +/- 2.0 a.u., the 8-phasic 6.9 +/- 1.6 a.u., and the 8-phasic with 5-us delays 25.4 +/- 2.8 a.u.
outcomes.quote: Bipolar signals started with exactly the same pulse (600 ns, 15 kV/cm) but caused significantly weaker effects (p<0.001). By the end of recording, YP signal reached only 20.8±2.0 a.u. for the 4-phasic signal; 6.9±1.6 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal; and 25.4±2.8 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal with 5-μs delays between phases.

statistics.about: each bipolar signal against the single unipolar pulse, end of recording
statistics.test: not named for single cells (Methods 2.2 names none; Methods 2.4 names a two-sided Student's t-test)

outcomes.notes: As fig4-sham-no-uptake, the single-cell data of Fig. 4 are in none of the datasets.

outcomes.statement: The 8-phasic signal with no delays causes about 20-fold weaker electroporation than a single unipolar pulse and is the most efficient at cancellation; the 4-phasic signal and the delayed 8-phasic signal cancel 4 to 5-fold.
outcomes.source: Figure 4 legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Results 3.4, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: identified the 8-phasic bipolar signal as the most efficient at cancellation (~20-fold) ... the other two types of bipolar signals which were less efficient at cancellation (4–5-fold, Fig. 4 ) ... Note that applying the 8-phasic bipolar signal with no inter-phase delays caused about 20-fold weaker electroporation than a single unipolar pulse
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-unipolar-strongest and fig4-bipolar-weaker, whose single-cell data are in none of the datasets.

outcomes.statement: Without rotation, 40 unipolar trains from e1 cause much stronger electroporation throughout the array than 40 Packet 2 packets started from e1, and the uptake after trains follows the field strength distribution.
outcomes.quote: The lack of cancellation caused a much stronger electroporation throughout the array, and the distribution of YP uptake expectedly followed the electric field strength distribution in Fig. 3C .
outcomes.notes: Along the e1 to e3 diagonal (4 packet and 4 train dishes, 000686), trains exceed packets at the e1 end (3.03 times, p = 0.0093) and in the centre (2.02 times, p = 0.0034), and the train profile falls from the e1 end to the centre (18094 against 7086 a.u., paired p = 0.0076, unpaired p = 0.0015), in all 16 readings. At the e3 end the trains are 0.75 times the packets (p = 0.40) in the main reading and not stronger in any reading. The criterion requires all three places and names no partial outcome, so the claim is not reproduced. The e3 end ROIs lie inside the image and are 2.0 to 4.2 times the dish's cell-free level in the train dishes (2.2 to 5.0 in the packet dishes), with no pixel at or below it; YO-PRO-1 cannot tell unaffected cells from bare glass.
deviations: The files do not say which needle is e1. e1 is taken as the needle whose outer quarter of the half-diagonal is brightest in the train dishes (only e1 is energized with trains); it is the upper right needle in all four train dishes and in all four packet dishes, and is used for both groups.
ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 on electrode squares found in the images, at an assumed pixel size of 0.65 um (10x objective, ORCA-Flash4 camera, Methods 2.4); the files give none.

outcomes.statement: Without rotation, Packet 2 enhances electroporation in the center of the array despite the weakening of the field with distance from e1, but uptake near e1 stays stronger than in the center.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, Packet 2 enhanced electroporation in the center of the array, despite gradual weakening of the electric field with distance from e1. However, the bipolar cancellation only partially offset the electric field weakening, and electroporation near e1 remained stronger than in the center.
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) of the enhancement holds by the paired test (O8) in all 16 readings, the packet centre being above the trough on the e1 side (3512 against 1326 a.u. at 1.03 mm; p = 0.016 paired, 0.017 unpaired). Reading (b) does not hold (centre over e1 end 0.89 for packets against 0.40 for trains, p = 0.10). The second part fails in every reading, the e1 end being above the centre without significance (5968 against 3512 a.u., p = 0.47 paired, 0.39 unpaired); in 2 of the 4 dishes the centre is the brighter.
deviations: e1 as in fig5a-trains-stronger; ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: With rotation (1P x 40), Packet 2 smears the effect at the perimeter and brings out a remote effect in the center, while the same rotation of unipolar trains (1T x 40) leaves a void of electroporation in the center.
outcomes.quote: Rotation with Packet 2 “smeared” the electroporation effect at the perimeter and emphasized the remote effect in the center. This remote effect contrasted with a void of electroporation in the center when the pulse train was applied in the same manner instead of the packet.
outcomes.notes: Tested; the readings disagree and no reading has a basis to be adopted. With the paired test, the 1P x 40 centre is above its trough in 96% of 48 readings (main 2526 against 1050 a.u. at 2.13 mm, p = 0.016). The 1T x 40 void, read as the centre below the most peripheral ROI (5376 against 11473 a.u.), holds by the paired test in 62% of readings and fails in the main one (p = 0.055); the centre ROI is the lowest point of the 1T x 40 profile in 8%. The two supported readings differ only in the ROI count (O1): the claim fails with 92 ROIs per diagonal and holds with the count split over the diagonals (void p = 0.020). With the unpaired test it holds in 98% of readings. Open for the paper's authors: how the ROIs were laid out (finding methods_unavailable).
deviations: Where the readings of a test disagree, the outcome is the one all the readings with a basis in the paper or the claims file give (ROI width w1, a standard choice; both diagonals, from the Fig. 5B legend; the ROI on the centre, per-dish normalization, raw intensity, per-dish ROI means, paired tests inside a dish, an assumption; cc.SUPPORTED_FIG5), with the ROI count (O1) and end ROI (O4) varied; where those disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.
ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the most peripheral ROI (100%), rotated Packet 2 and rotated trains show sharply different spatial distributions, the packet's center being relatively high and the trains' relatively low.
outcomes.quote: The striking difference in the spatial distribution of electroporation between the CANCAN and control treatments is appreciated best by comparing the normalized fluorescence data, when the emission intensity in the most peripheral (closest to the electrode) ROI is taken as 100% ( Fig. 5C ).
outcomes.notes: Blocked because it depends on fig5b-rotation-center-peak, blocked as methods_underspecified. Its own test holds: normalized centre 213% for 1P x 40 against 57% for 1T x 40 (Student p = 0.0088, Welch p = 0.018), significant in all 32 readings, and the 1P x 40 centre is above 100% in all of them.
deviations: ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: Raising the total number of rotated Packet 2 packets from 4 (1Px4) to 20 (5Px4) and 40 (10Px4) strongly raises YP uptake throughout the array, and a central peak is discernible for every treatment.
outcomes.quote: Increasing the total number of applied packets from 4 to 20 and 40 profoundly enhanced the electroporative YP dye uptake throughout the electrode array ( Fig. 6A ). The peak of electroporation in the center was clearly discernable for all tested treatments.
outcomes.notes: 000875 holds 3 dishes per treatment, all at 3.2 kV in the small array (O11). Uptake rises from 4 to 20 to 40 packets at the most peripheral ROI (558, 3515, 9472 a.u.), the trough (458, 1189, 1567) and the centre (726, 2366, 5800), and 40 exceed 4 at each place (p = 0.0027, 0.0014, 0.00015), in all 48 readings. By the paired test the centre is above the trough for 10Px4 in 83% of readings (main p = 0.0024) but for 1Px4 in none (main p = 0.20) and for 5Px4 in 8% (p = 0.13); for every treatment in none, paired or unpaired. The criterion's partial outcome names only a rise at one or two places; here the rise holds at all three and the peak test fails for two treatments, which is read as partial. This gap is asked of a reader (questions/pakhomov-2023.yaml). With the diagonals (O2) varied the peak test still fails for every treatment in all 6 supported readings.
deviations: The criterion gives no outcome for a rise at all three places with the peak test failing for some treatments. It is read as partially reproduced, an assumption, since the rise holds and part of the claim's statement does not.
ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

Where the readings of a test disagree, the outcome is the one all the supported readings give (ROI width w1, a standard choice; the ROI on the centre; per-dish normalization; raw intensity; per-dish ROI means; paired tests inside a dish, an assumption; cc.SUPPORTED), with the ROI count (O1), the end ROI (O4) and, outside Fig. 5, the diagonals (O2) varied; where those disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

outcomes.statement: The central peak is almost twofold brighter than the periphery for 1Px4, and about the same as the periphery for 5Px4 and 10Px4.
outcomes.quote: Its brightness was almost twofold higher than at the periphery for a single packet was applied 4 times from different directions, or about the same as at the periphery for the rotation of 5 and 10 packets ( Fig. 6B ).
outcomes.notes: Main reading 128% (1Px4), 70% (5Px4) and 64% (10Px4). No reading of 576 puts all three within tolerance. In 6 readings, all with background subtraction (O6 b), raw values, w1 and the d1 diagonal, 1Px4 is within tolerance (183 to 186%) and above both others, the criterion's partial outcome. 1Px4 is the highest of the three in 99% of readings. Over readings 1Px4 spans 105 to 186%, 5Px4 35 to 170%, 10Px4 27 to 110%.
deviations: ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel; background for O6 b is the 1st percentile of the image inside the electrode square, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: For all three packet numbers, the least affected area between the center and the electrodes shows about 2-fold lower fluorescence than the center.
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, the least affected area of the cell monolayer (between the center and the electrodes) showed about 2-fold lower fluorescence intensity than in the center for all the treatments.
outcomes.notes: Centre over trough in the main reading is 1.59 (1Px4), 1.99 (5Px4) and 3.70 (10Px4), given as measured in that order. No reading of 288 puts all three in 1.8 to 2.2; 114 put one or two in range with all above 1, the criterion's partial outcome. The ratio grows with the number of packets in the main reading.
deviations: ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: The central peak becomes narrower with more packets.
outcomes.quote: Also, the central peak appeared narrower (sharper) with increasing the number of packets.
outcomes.notes: Width at half height above the trough on the mean normalized profile falls from 0.657 mm (1Px4) to 0.636 mm (5Px4) to 0.438 mm (10Px4) in the main reading and in 87% of 144 readings of this width. With the diagonals (O2) varied, as the claims file's statement that the paper does not say for Figs. 6 to 9 requires, it falls in 4 of the 6 supported readings (both diagonals, and d2); on the d1 diagonal 5Px4 is wider than 1Px4 under both ROI counts (0.658, 0.804, 0.249 mm and 0.697, 0.733, 0.396 mm), the partial outcome. The supported readings give reproduced and partially reproduced, and the paper gives no basis to choose the diagonal, so the claim is blocked. 10Px4 is narrower than 1Px4 in all six. The distance between troughs, the criterion's reading (b), falls in order in 42% of its readings and in 2 of the 6 supported ones, not in the main reading (1.471, 1.758, 1.614 mm). Rounds 1 and 2 verified reproduced, with both diagonals fixed and reading (a) assumed; round 3 agreed to the change to blocked. Open for the paper's authors, the diagonals (finding methods_unavailable).
deviations: The paper defines no width, and the criterion's two readings disagree in part. Reading (a), the full width at half height above the trough, the criterion's first reading and the usual measure of a peak's width, is the one reported; with the diagonals varied it splits the supported readings on its own.

Where the readings of a test disagree, the outcome is the one all the supported readings give (ROI width w1, a standard choice; the ROI on the centre; per-dish normalization; raw intensity; per-dish ROI means; paired tests inside a dish, an assumption; cc.SUPPORTED), with the ROI count (O1), the end ROI (O4) and, outside Fig. 5, the diagonals (O2) varied; where those disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

outcomes.statement: With 1Px4 in the small array, raising the first-pulse amplitude from 2.4 to 5.6 kV raises YP fluorescence 15.5 times at the most peripheral point, 16.2 times half-way to the center and 16.8 times in the center.
outcomes.quote: For example, when the first pulse amplitude was increased from 2.4 to 5.6 kV ... YP fluorescence increased 15.5 times at the most peripheral point; 16.2 times half-way to the center; and 16.8 times in the center ( Fig. 7A ).
outcomes.notes: Small array, 1Px4, 2.4 kV (4 dishes) against 5.6 kV (3 dishes). The main reading gives 6.66 at the most peripheral ROI, 5.71 half-way and 7.33 in the centre, less than half the paper's 15.5, 16.2 and 16.8. Over 288 readings the ratios span 5.26 to 13.96, 4.82 to 15.47 and 5.91 to 15.27. No reading has all three within 10%; 10 readings, all background-subtracted and on the d2 diagonal, have one within 10%, the criterion's partial outcome.
deviations: 001025 holds 4 dishes at 2.4 kV where the paper gives n = 3; all 4 are used.
ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the most peripheral ROI, the profiles for different amplitudes fully overlap; amplitude changes the degree of electroporation but not its spatial distribution.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, changing nsEP amplitude affected the degree of electroporation but not its spatial distribution ( Fig. 7 ). ... When the YP emission was normalized to the most peripheral ROI, the data for different nsEP amplitudes fully overlapped ( Fig. 7B ).
outcomes.notes: Tested; the readings disagree and no reading has a basis to be adopted. Voltages 2.4, 3.2, 4.0, 4.8 and 5.6 kV (4, 3, 3, 3, 3 dishes). Over 96 readings no pair differs in 27%. Of the 12 supported readings (O1 x O2 x O4), only the main one finds no pair (20 tests, smallest p = 0.052, 2.4 against 4.8 kV at the centre); with O1 b two pairs differ (2.4 against 4.8 kV, p = 0.026; 2.4 against 5.6 kV, p = 0.0051, both at the centre), and the others one to three. With raw intensity no pair differs in 2% of readings. Under both O1 readings the error-bar rule finds 3 or 4 of 20 pairs different and a one-way ANOVA of per-dish normalized centres finds a voltage effect (p = 0.028 and 0.021); on each dish's mean normalized profile it does not (p = 0.26 and 0.12). The normalized centre at 4.8 kV is 229% (dishes 136, 232, 318%) against 117 to 129% at the other voltages. Leaving out any one of the four 2.4 kV dishes leaves the supported readings split (no pair differing in 25% of them). Open for the paper's authors: the ROI layout, the diagonals and the end ROI (finding methods_unavailable).
deviations: 001025 holds 4 dishes at 2.4 kV where the Fig. 7 legend gives n = 3; all 4 are used, and each is left out in turn as a check.

Where the readings of a test disagree, the outcome is the one all the supported readings give (ROI width w1, a standard choice; the ROI on the centre; per-dish normalization; raw intensity; per-dish ROI means; paired tests inside a dish, an assumption; cc.SUPPORTED), with the ROI count (O1), the end ROI (O4) and, outside Fig. 5, the diagonals (O2) varied; where those disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.
ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: The independence of the normalized distribution from amplitude also holds when rotating multiple packets (10Px4) in the larger array.
outcomes.quote: The findings held true for rotating multiple packets and when using the larger array ( Fig. 7C and D ). Overall, our results show that NG-CANCAN targeting of electroporation does not depend on nsEP amplitude, at least within the studied amplitude range.
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 10Px4 on the large array at 4.8 kV (2 dishes) and 6.4 kV (3 dishes). Normalized centres 204% and 198% (p = 0.95); half-way they differ by 53 percentage points (p = 0.14). No pair differs in 96% of 96 readings. With the diagonals (O2) varied, 11 of 12 supported readings find no pair and one, on the d1 diagonal with 92 ROIs and the mean of the end ROIs, finds one (p = 0.037); every reading with a pair differing is on d1. The supported readings disagree and the paper gives no basis to choose the diagonal, the rule applied to fig7b-targeting-independent-of-amplitude, so the claim is blocked; the split is thin (1 of 12). Rounds 1 and 2 verified reproduced with both diagonals fixed; round 3 agreed to the change to blocked. The error-bar rule finds none. The test has little power: with a pooled s.d. of 91 percentage points, a difference of about 353 points in the normalized centre would be needed for 80% power. Uptake in a.u. rises 3.39 times at the most peripheral ROI and 4.03 times in the centre from 4.8 to 6.4 kV.
deviations: Two voltages only, with 2 dishes at 4.8 kV where the paper gives n = 3.

Where the readings of a test disagree, the outcome is the one all the supported readings give (ROI width w1, a standard choice; the ROI on the centre; per-dish normalization; raw intensity; per-dish ROI means; paired tests inside a dish, an assumption; cc.SUPPORTED), with the ROI count (O1), the end ROI (O4) and, outside Fig. 5, the diagonals (O2) varied; where those disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

outcomes.statement: Remote targeting, within the studied limits, depends neither on pulse amplitude nor on array size, so findings from small arrays can be extrapolated to larger inter-electrode distances.
outcomes.quote: the remote targeting, at least within studied limits, did not depend on either the electric pulse amplitude or array size ( Fig. 7 ). We infer that findings from small electrode arrays can be extrapolated to larger inter-electrode distances.
outcomes.notes: Blocked because it depends on fig7b-targeting-independent-of-amplitude, blocked as methods_underspecified; fig7cd-holds-for-large-array is blocked too, as its supported readings disagree on the diagonal. The normalized centres are 117 to 229% on the small array (1Px4, by voltage) and 198 to 204% on the large array (10Px4); packet number and array size are confounded, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Packets 1, 2 and 3 at 4 kV, rotated one cycle (1Px4), give the same YP uptake in the center of the array, 215 to 235 a.u.
outcomes.quote: All packets produced the same YP uptake in the center (215–235 a.u.)
outcomes.notes: Centres of Packets 1, 2 and 3 (3, 4, 3 dishes at 4 kV, small array) are 692, 378 and 401 a.u. in the main reading, given as measured in that order; no reading puts all three in 193.5 to 258.5 a.u. Packet 1 differs from Packet 2 (p = 0.0009) and Packet 3 (p = 0.0074), and some pair differs in all 192 readings on dish means. The files' a.u. may not be the paper's scale. Whether the paper's a.u. are on the scale of the deposited pixel values is asked of a reader.
deviations: ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel; packets read from the session descriptions, which define Protocol1 as 4 phases, Protocol2 as 8 phases without delay and Protocol3 as 8 phases with 5-us delays, Packets 1, 2 and 3 of Methods 2.3.

outcomes.statement: Packets 1 and 3 cause much more YP uptake near the electrodes (250 to 350 a.u.) than Packet 2 (about 120 a.u.), p < 0.01.
outcomes.quote: but Packets 1 and 3 caused drastically more YP uptake near the electrodes (250–350 a.u. vs ~120 a.u. for packet 1, p<0.01, Fig. 8A )

statistics.about: Packets 1 and 3 against Packet 2, near the electrodes

outcomes.notes: Most peripheral ROI, main reading, Packet 1 810, Packet 3 284 and Packet 2 525 a.u. (measured in that order, Packets 1 and 3 for the first expected value, then Packet 2). No reading puts the values in range (Packet 1 338 to 968, Packet 2 185 to 589, Packet 3 83 to 338 a.u. over readings). Packet 3 is below Packet 2 (p = 0.0015), and Packet 1 above it at p = 0.025, above 0.01; both tests hold in none of 192 readings.
deviations: The text's "~120 a.u. for packet 1" is read as Packet 2, as the claims file does.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the most peripheral ROI, YP emission in the center is 183% for Packet 2 and drops to 83% for Packet 3 and 74% for Packet 1.
outcomes.quote: The superiority of Packet 2 for CANCAN targeting is highlighted by the drop of normalized YP emission in the center from 183% for Packet 2 to 83% and 74% for Packets 3 and 1, respectively ( Fig. 8B ).
outcomes.notes: Normalized centre in the main reading, Packet 2 73%, Packet 3 141%, Packet 1 88% (measured in the claim's order). No reading puts all three within 10%, and Packet 3 has the highest normalized centre in every reading. The session descriptions confirm the labels (Protocol2, 8 phases without delay; Protocol3, 8 phases with 5-us delays). With the Protocol 2 and 3 labels exchanged, a variant the files do not support, Packet 2 would be highest in every reading and 19 of 576 readings would put all three within 10%.
deviations: ROIs rebuilt from Methods 2.4 at an assumed 0.65 um pixel.

outcomes.statement: The bipolar signal with the strongest cancellation between two electrodes (8-phasic, Fig. 4) gives the most efficient remote targeting in the quadrupole (Packet 2, Fig. 8).
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 3; Results 3.4, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figures 4 and 8
outcomes.quote: Three packets for CANCAN targeting were designed to produce three types of bipolar signals near electrodes and we showed that, indeed, the strongest bipolar cancellation has led to the most efficient remote targeting ( Figs. 4 and 8 ).
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-twenty-fold-cancellation, whose single-cell data of Fig. 4 are in none of the datasets. On the Fig. 8 side alone, the dishes the files label Packet 3 (not Packet 2) give the highest normalized centre in every reading (fig8b-packet2-best-targeting).

outcomes.statement: With the large array lifted 1, 2 and 3 mm above the monolayer, YP emission near the electrodes falls 2.4, 6.4 and 9 times against electrodes touching the cells, while in the center it falls only 1.02, 1.4 and 3.8 times.
outcomes.quote: Specifically, YP emission near the electrodes decreased 2.4, 6.4, and 9 times with 1-, 2- and 3-mm gaps (as compared to electrodes being in the same plane with cells); in the center, it decreased just 1.02, 1.4, and 3.8 times, respectively.
outcomes.notes: 3 dishes per gap. Main reading, near the electrodes 2.38, 4.68 and 8.20 times with 1, 2 and 3 mm (paper 2.4, 6.4, 9), in the centre 1.06, 1.91 and 4.07 (paper 1.02, 1.4, 3.8). No reading has all six within 10% (at most 4, in the main reading). The near-electrode ratio exceeds the centre ratio at every gap in 88% of 576 readings, including the main one.
deviations: For the 2 and 3 mm gaps the electrodes leave no footprint in the YO-PRO-1 image; the square is completed from two needle marks in the second channel. Where both methods apply (9 dishes with clear footprints) their centres differ by 0.09 mm (median), at most 0.23 mm. On the lifted dishes the inner 1 mm mean differs by at most 29% between the two squares, and the single centre ROI by up to 2.7 times.

outcomes.statement: The faster fading near the electrodes raises targeting efficiency (center over periphery) to as much as 600% with a 2-mm gap.
outcomes.quote: Such disproportionally faster fading of the effect near electrodes boosted the CANCAN targeting efficiency (measured as a ratio of the effect in the center and at the periphery) to as much as 600% for the 2-mm gap ( Fig. 9B ).
outcomes.notes: Normalized centre in the main reading 198, 466, 541 and 382% at 0, 1, 2 and 3 mm; the 2 mm value is within 540 to 660% and the largest. This holds in 107 of 576 readings, and the 2 mm value is the largest of the four in 84%.
deviations: Square for the 2 and 3 mm dishes from the needle marks, as in fig9a-gap-reduces-periphery-more.

outcomes.statement: With the electrodes placed above the monolayer, electroporation is restricted almost exclusively to the center of the array.
outcomes.quote: Consistent with these measurements, YP fluorescence images in Fig. 9C show that electroporation is restricted almost exclusively to the remote target (center) when electrodes are placed above the cell monolayer.
outcomes.notes: By the paired test (O8) the centre is above the most peripheral ROI at 1 mm (p = 0.021) but not at 2 mm (p = 0.051) or 3 mm (p = 0.34) in the main reading; all three gaps hold in 8% of readings and in none of the 12 supported ones with the diagonals varied (25% unpaired). At 2 mm alone the paired test holds in 92% of readings. The centre is the highest point of the mean profile at all three gaps in none of 96 readings (main reading maximum at 0.44 mm at 2 mm). The 3 mm dishes have centre values of 660, 3782 and 592 a.u. Whether a strict maximum at ROI resolution is intended is asked of a reader.
deviations: Square for the 2 and 3 mm dishes from the needle marks, as in fig9a-gap-reduces-periphery-more.

findings.statement: None of the five dandisets holds the single-cell time-lapse images of Fig. 4 (Methods 2.2) or the electric field simulations of Fig. 3, so six of the paper's claims cannot be tested.

The files give no pixel size (ImageSeries resolution is -1 in 000686 and 000875 and 1 or 96 in the other three, with no field of view), no electrode positions, no ROIs, no array size and no position of electrode e1. All have to be inferred from the images. An assumed 0.65 um pixel gives a large-array diagonal of 8.25 mm between needle edges (paper 8.4 mm).
17 files of 001025 and 001028 hold a second frame (described as Channels FITC, DAPI) that no description explains. It shows dark marks at the upper needles.
The subject species of 000686 and 000875 is NCBITaxon 9913 (Bos taurus) for CHO cells, which are Chinese hamster (NCBITaxon 10029, as given in the other three dandisets).

Six dishes are deposited twice with identical pixel data, in two dandisets each (000875 dishes 23, 24, 25 as 001025 sub-23, sub-24, sub-25 obj-1of0oop; 001025 sub-04, 07, 11 as 001028 sub-04, 07, 11), consistent with their use in two figures. No dandiset holds a duplicate inside itself.
001025 holds 4 small-array dishes at 2.4 kV and 2 large-array dishes at 4.8 kV, where the paper gives n = 3 for Fig. 7; which dishes the paper used is not stated.

In 001027 the dishes labelled Protocol3, which the session descriptions define as 8 phases with 5-us delays (Packet 3 of Methods 2.3), give the highest normalized centre of the three packets in every reading, where the paper reports the highest for Packet 2.

The assets summary of 001027 names the species "Cricetulus griseus - Cricetulus aureus" for one cell line (CHO, NCBITaxon 10029, Chinese hamster), and each subject is a dish with age P1D, which does not apply to a cell line. The ImageSeries description of dish 10 gives an unknown microscope, detector and objective, where the other nine name the Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 and a 10x objective, and its session starts on 18 March 2021 at 18:50, where the other Packet 2 and 3 dishes start on 17 March between 11:36 and 13:03. The files record no exposure or gain, and the background inside the electrode footprints of the three Packet 1 dishes, imaged on 24 March 2021, is 308.9 a.u., 1.94 times that of the other seven (161.1 and 150.0 a.u. on 17 and 18 March), so a.u. values may not be comparable between imaging days.

outcomes.note: The earlier attempt used 001027 only, which holds no Fig. 6 dishes, and blocked the claim as data_missing. This attempt tested it on 000875, which was published before the earlier attempt. The change comes from the protocol (pilot-14 files records by paper and uses every dataset the paper rests on) and the claims file written under it, which names all five dandisets.

As for fig6a-more-packets-more-uptake, the earlier attempt had only 001027, which holds no Fig. 9 dishes. This attempt tested the claim on 001028 under pilot-14 and its claims file for the whole paper; the dataset did not change.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1: the first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module cancan.py and the claims file, with the paper's full text (PMC10247516). The verifier read the archive's asset lists and session descriptions and tested dish_profiles, corner_names, dish_values and peak_width on synthetic images. Also in reply, not tied to one claim: O3 (b) now averages the first ROIs of the half-diagonals in use (problem 9); the LOESS fit is made on the profile mirrored about the centre (problem 8); the 0.65 um pixel size is kept (problem 11, judged reasonable). Flat-field tiling was not quantified, and figure-only values were not compared (no PDF).

disagreements.reason: Trains exceed packets at the e1 end and the centre in 16/16 readings, but not at the e3 end (ratio 0.75, p = 0.40). The criterion requires all three places, so it fails. Problem 1: in the four 40-train dishes the BL needle taken as e3 sits in a dark, cell-free looking area, `_roi_means` drops an ROI only when more than 20% of its pixels are exactly 0, so the e3 values may come from off-monolayer pixels, and nothing checks ROI coverage.

At least one voltage pair differs in 74% of readings (98% without background subtraction). The paper's own error-bar rule finds 3 pairs differing under the main reading. The 4.8 kV normalized centre is 229% against about 120% at the other voltages. The main reading, with no pair differing (min p = 0.052), is an outlier among the readings (problem 2). Problem 6: the ANOVA variant treats each ROI as independent (pseudoreplication).
Its criterion needs both fig7b and fig7cd reproduced, and fig7b is not.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2: the full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, the helper module cancan.py, the claims file, the attempt record and the paper's full text. Also in reply, not tied to one claim: cc.SUPPORTED no longer fixes both diagonals (O2 a) outside Fig. 5, where the claims file says the paper does not say (cc.SUPPORTED_FIG5 keeps it for Fig. 5); the notebook now calls w1, O3 a and the paired test standard choices or assumptions, not readings from the paper; the Summary no longer infers that the paper's a.u. scale differs (with background subtracted the Fig. 8 centres are 154 to 418 a.u.) and says it is asked of a reader; the README says 17 files hold a second channel; the cell 19 panel titles are no longer hidden; the round-1 responses on fig6a and fig9c are corrected. The trough bias, the flat-field tiling and the figure-only values remain open, as the report says, with no bearing on a conclusion.

disagreements.reason: Agrees only partly. The assumption and the low power are stated, but "supported" fixes O2 = a, both diagonals, on the basis of the Fig. 5B legend, where the claims file says that for Figs. 6 to 9 "the paper does not say". The only readings where a pair differs are on the d1 diagonal (cell 50, d1 max 1 pair), so the agreement among the supported readings depends on a basis the claims file does not give. If O2 has no basis outside Fig. 5 the supported readings may disagree, and the claim could then be blocked rather than reproduced.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 3: the two proposed changes of outcome (fig6-peak-narrower and fig7cd-holds-for-large-array) and the analysis behind them in the executed notebook (cells 13, 40 and 50), with the claims file and the paper. The other 22 outcomes carry no proposal and were not reviewed.

paper_notes.statement: Questions for the paper's authors. (1) How were the 92 or 224 ROIs laid out (per diagonal or split over both diagonals), how wide were they, and along which diagonals were Figs. 6 to 9 measured? The outcomes of Figs. 5B, 6 (peak width), 7B and 7C, D depend on it. (2) Was the most peripheral value the mean of the end ROIs of the averaged profile, or was each half-diagonal normalized to its own end? (3) How was the geometric centre located, especially with electrodes lifted 2 and 3 mm, where no footprint shows? (4) Was a background subtracted from the monolayer images, and are the a.u. values of the text (215 to 235 a.u. in the Fig. 8 centre) raw pixel values of the deposited images? (5) Were comparisons within the same dishes (centre against periphery or trough) paired or unpaired? (6) Which needle in the images is e1? (7) Were values in the text read from ROI means or from the LOESS fits, and with what span? The attempt ran every reading the claims file lists; where tests disagreed it adopted the readings with a basis in the paper and blocked the claims where those still disagreed.

entries.name: pakhomov-2023
entries.title: Next generation CANCAN focusing of electroporation (Pakhomov et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the monolayer findings of Pakhomov, Gudvangen, Mangalanathan, Kondratiev, Redondo and Semenov (2023) on dandisets 000686, 000875, 001025, 001027 and 001028, which hold the stitched YO-PRO-1 images of the CHO monolayers of Figures 5 to 9, one dish per file. The electrode squares are found in the images and the ROIs of Methods 2.4 are rebuilt from them. The single-cell time lapse of Figure 4 and the field simulations of Figure 3 are in none of the datasets.
